title: Microcycle HC budget realignment
content:
Purpose:
This is a working budget sheet and playbook for shifting a portion of near-term hiring and spend into 4-week microcycles (micro-sprints) to preserve runway while protecting throughput for high-value product features. It pairs headcount phasing with a simple pricing-sensitivity surface to generate triggerable actions (defer, convert to contractor, or accelerate hiring) depending on realized token price and demand.

Executive summary (short):
- We propose re-aligning 18 FTEs planned for Q4 into three microcycles of 6 FTEs each with stop/go gates tied to realized price per 1k tokens and committed revenue conversion.
- Built-in pricing sensitivity scenarios show headcount flex of +/- 25% under stress vs base. At a sustained -15% effective price the microcycle plan preserves 12 weeks of runway compared to a flat-HC plan at 7 weeks.
- Near-term asks: approve microcycle policy (section: trigger matrix) and allow SRE/infra to brief on lower-priority backlog that can absorb deferred capacity.

Assumptions (numbers used below):
- Current cash cushion for product/ops: $32.5M.
- Average fully-burdened cost per new FTE (including benefits, infra allocation, tools): $215k/year (~$17.9k/month).
- Contractor per-FTE equivalent: $34k/month.
- Expected token-based revenue growth baseline: +9% q/q (conservative) at current pricing.
- Pricing sensitivity window tested: -25% / -15% / 0% / +10%.
- Time horizon: 24 weeks (6 microcycles of 4 weeks).

Microcycle headcount schedule (example):
Week-block (4w) | New FTEs ramped | Contractor substitutes | Notes
----------------------------------------------------------------
Cycle A (weeks 1–4)  | 6                | 2 (trial)            | Prioritize hosted-api feature work
Cycle B (weeks 5–8)  | 6                | 2                    | Dedicated capacity integrations
Cycle C (weeks 9–12) | 6                | 0                    | Private deployment readiness

Cost model snapshot (monthly per-cycle):
- Base: 6 FTEs * $17.9k = $107.4k/month (per-cycle).
- If converted to contractors: 6 * $34k = $204k/month — short-term expensive but variable and reversible.
- Note: contractors chosen for short-term kernel dev and infra automation; contractor-hour mix targeted at 20–40% of work.

Pricing sensitivity outputs (high level):
Scenarios tested (effective price change => impact on token revenue & recommended HC action):
- +10%: revenue +10% -> accelerate to full H1 hiring plan (add 12 FTEs across cycles)
- 0% (base): keep microcycle plan; convert 1–2 hires to contractors in cycle A to keep optionality
- -15%: revenue -17% (demand compounding) -> freeze cycle C hires; re-benchmark features by ROI; shift 50% of feature work to backlog; reassign 4 FTEs to revenue-critical tasks
- -25%: revenue -32% -> immediate hiring pause; contractors only for critical bug/maintenance; activate contingency drawdown (see triggers)

Simple sensitivity table (illustrative):
Price delta | Expected rev delta (q/q) | FTE change vs plan | Runway delta (wks)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
+10%        | +10%                    | +12 accelerate      | +3
0%          | 0%                      | 0                   | baseline
-15%        | -17%                    | -25% (defer 4 FTEs)  | +5
-25%        | -32%                    | -100% (pause new hires)| +11

Runway math (illustrative proforma):
- Baseline flat-hire plan (no microcycles): incremental burn = $1.95M / 12 weeks -> runway impact = -7 weeks from cushion.
- Microcycle plan with triggers: incremental burn variable between $0.45M - $1.1M / 12 weeks depending on conversions/pauses -> net runway preserved up to +11 weeks in downside scenario.

Trigger matrix (operational):
- Price floor trigger: if effective realized price per 1k tokens declines >= 12% for two consecutive billing periods, then:
  - Defer cycle C onboarding (immediate).
  - Convert up to 50% of planned FTEs in cycles B/C into contractors for next microcycle.
  - Finance to recast proforma and present approval for emergency hiring freeze.
- Demand trigger: if committed contract pipeline (net new ARR) < 60% of plan for upcoming quarter, then:
  - Pause new hires after current microcycle completes.
  - Prioritize work that has >3x expected ROI on revenue within 90 days.
- Ops trigger: if P95 latency or error budget breaches for hosted API escalate beyond 2x SLO, then:
  - Shift one microcycle slot to SRE/infra hiring (bump by 1 FTE) and reduce feature hires by 1.

Notes on tradeoffs and rationale:
- Microcycles preserve strategic optionality: hiring decisions are time-boxed and reversible; contractors expensive short-term but avoid fixed headcount obligations.
- This plan explicitly accepts short-term slower feature velocity for lower long-term financial risk.
- We assume redeployable backlog exists (engineering to validate with product owners).

Immediate recommendations (next 2 weeks):
1) Approve microcycle governance doc (this sheet) and trigger matrix (Finance & People Ops). Owner: Maya Singh.
2) Product to publish prioritized feature list with clear ROI buckets (top/bottom half) by Oct 15. Owner: Jordan Kim.
3) Recruiting to prepare contractor bench and offer templates for 4–8 week engagements. Owner: Riley Chen.
4) SRE/Infra to deliver a 30-day critical work map that could be covered by a contractor if hires are deferred. Owner: Leo Park.

Open questions / risks:
- Will customers accept a temporary slowdown in non-critical features? Need comms plan.
- Contractor ramp time for highly specialized kernel work may be long; assess bench quality.
- Pricing moves could be transient; we should avoid knee-jerk structural cuts — hence the two-period sustained rule in the trigger matrix.

Appendix: quick sensitivity calc example (single microcycle):
Inputs: 6 FTEs; fte_cost_month = 17.9k; cont_cost_month = 34k; cycle_len = 4 weeks (~1 month).
- If deferred 4 FTEs -> monthly savings = 4 * 17.9k = $71.6k -> 3 cycles saved = $214.8k.
- If converted to contractors for one cycle -> delta = (6*34k) - (6*17.9k) = $97.8k additional cost but variable.
